prompt: Increasing awareness of the need for environmental controls is one way that marketing has
explanation: Improved the quality of life. Marketing has improved the quality of life by encouraging the development of safer, better goods and services. In addition, marketing has increased awareness of the need for environmental controls to protect our physical surroundings, which has led to an improvement in our existence. Making people aware of the need for environmental controls does not add usefulness to products or make buying more convenient, although those are other benefits of marketing. Marketing does not regulate the standard of living but usually helps to raise it by improving the general conditions in which people live.

prompt: When authority for all purchasing activities lies with one department or individual in a retail chain, this is referred to as a __________ purchasing structure.
explanation: Centralized. Centralized purchasing funnels the responsibilities for the firm's purchasing to one department or individual. In a decentralized purchasing structure, each department is responsible for its own purchasing. A departmentalized purchasing structure is a combination of these two purchasing structures. Concentrated is not a type of purchasing structure.

prompt: A toy store would not be able to develop yearly operating budgets without accurate
explanation: Accounting systems. Toy store managers rely on accurate accounting information to help them make decisions about the future of the toy store. Accurate accounting systems tell managers how much money will be available for operating expenses and predict the amount of expected income. Managers need this information to decide how to allocate funds in order to make a profit. Marketing plans help the business promote and sell its goods and services. Distribution systems move goods to the consumer. Production plans control how goods will be produced.

prompt: Which of the following statements is true about strategic planning:
choices: It involves planning for the next three-to-five years.
It involves short-term planning for the next six months.
It is a supervisory technique for improving employee performance.
It is used primarily by departments that do not meet company goals.
explanation: It involves planning for the next three-to-five years. Strategic planning is long-range planning for the company as a whole and is a responsibility of top-level management. Short-term planning is done by lower level managers. Strategic planning is not a supervisory technique nor is it limited to departments that are not performing well.

prompt: A large retail chain sells stock in its company. This is an example of which of the following types of business ownership:
explanation: Corporation. A corporation is a business (e.g., large retail chain) that is owned by its shareholders who buy stocks in the company. Corporations are operated under written permission from the states or provinces in which they operate. A sole proprietorship is a business owned and operated by one person. A partnership is owned by two or more people. A franchisee purchases the rights to operate a business using the parent company's (franchisor's) name.

prompt: One of the ways technology puts money in retailers' accounts more quickly is through
explanation: Customers' use of debit cards. Most retailers now accept debit cards, a form of electronic payment from customers. These are also called check cards. When customers use debit cards, the amount of the purchase is automatically deducted from the customer's checking account and transferred into the retailer's account. This makes funds available to retailers immediately and greatly improves their cash flow. When customers use checks, retailers must wait for them to "clear," or to be deposited in the bank and collected from customers' accounts. This may take a day or two or several days. Smart cards are "prepaid" cards from which purchase amounts are deducted. Not all retailers accept smart cards for payment. Virtual deposit processes are not in use. Retailers must still physically deposit cash and checks at the bank.

prompt: Large retailers often use presentation software to develop computerized training materials that contain interactive buttons that allow employees to
explanation: Test themselves. Presentation software enables large retailers to develop materials that contain interactive buttons that allow employees to test themselves on their knowledge and understanding of the material. Large retailers often develop this type of computerized training materials because it allows employees to learn at their own pace, test themselves, and review the material if necessary. Employees can read a question or view an action on a computer screen and respond by clicking on an interactive button. The computer quickly processes the information and advises the employees if their answers are correct. Large retailers do not develop computerized training materials that contain interactive buttons in order to allow employees to study together, access databases, or conduct research.

prompt: One way that the technology of online shopping impacts retailing is by allowing retailers to
choices: sell items that have low demand.
explanation: Sell items that have low demand. Most retailers do not have the shelf space in their stores to carry all the items that customers might want to buy. They must limit the selection to those items that are in the most demand. However, the technology of online shopping allows retailers to sell items that have low demand and thereby meet the needs of a wider range of customers. When a customer orders such an item online, the retailer can ship it from storage or purchase it from a distributor. There is no need to maintain a large inventory, and the retailer increases sales. The technology of online shopping does not allow retailers to offer extremely high discounts. Selling directly to customers usually involves meeting with them personally. Online shopping enables retailers to offer additional services to customers.

prompt: Is it possible to buy insurance to protect your belongings if you don't own your home, but lease it from someone else?
choices: Yes, you can buy renter's insurance.
Yes, you can buy life insurance.
No, leased properties cannot be insured.
No, insurance must be purchased by the owner.
explanation: Yes, you can buy renter's insurance. Renter's insurance is a form of liability coverage that can be purchased by those who rent or lease property to cover their possessions. The owner of the property should buy homeowner's insurance to cover the property. Life insurance would not protect your belongings as it is not paid out until the death of the policyholder.

prompt: Before a business and a customer can enter into a valid contract, the offer to do something in return for payment must be
explanation: Accepted. Contracts are agreements between two or more parties stating that one party is to do something in return for something provided by another party. Several elements must be present for a contract to be valid. First, one party must make an offer to do something such as sell a product for a certain price and deliver it on a certain date. Then, the other party must accept that offer. A valid contract cannot be formed unless the offer is accepted. The offer may be made verbally or in writing. Express and implied are types of contracts that may be formed once the offer is accepted.

prompt: The law that requires the Val-u-rama Discount Store to hire, train, transfer, and promote employees without regard to race, color, gender, religion, or national origin is the __________ Act.
explanation: Civil Rights. The Civil Rights Act requires businesses (e.g., Val-u-rama Discount Store) to hire, train, transfer, and promote employees without regard to race, color, gender, religion, or national origin. The Robinson-Patman Act deals primarily with pricing practices. The Sherman Antitrust Act deals with monopolies and competition. The Federal Reserve Act created the Federal Reserve.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a good listening skill:
explanation: Asking appropriate questions. Being a good listener is important on the job and in other types of relationships. One way to be a good listener is to ask appropriate questions in order to clarify what the speaker is saying. For example, this means asking specific questions about how to perform a task if a manager is explaining a new job function. It does not mean continually interrupting the speaker with irrelevant comments or asking questions that do not pertain to the conversation. Good listeners look at the speakers and focus on what they are saying rather than thinking about a response.

prompt: Communicating by telephone is sometimes more difficult than communicating face-to-face because
choices: tone of voice is less important.
notes and references can be used.
explanation: Nonverbal cues are missing. Until telephones with visual components become commonplace, there will be no way to use body language and/or facial expression to help express the speaker's message. The fact that physical distractions can be removed and that notes and references can be used make telephone communication easier, not harder. A person's tone of voice is very important in both telephone communication and face-to-face communication.

prompt: Requests, directions, and information are often communicated in writing because messages sent in writing are less likely to be
explanation: Misunderstood. Clearly written communications can prevent problems that may be caused by poor listening or speaking skills. The written message can also be checked for clarity and accuracy before it is delivered. Both writing and speech can be friendly or businesslike in tone.

prompt: Why should a hardware store owner inform his/her employees that their e-mail will be monitored?
explanation: To respect their privacy. Some businesses, such as hardware stores, consider e-mail to be corporate property and routinely monitor the messages that employees send and receive. If a hardware store owner monitors e-mail, s/he should inform his/her employees in order to respect their privacy. Employees have the right to know if someone in the hardware store will read their e-mail so that they can decide the type of information they will include. They might not want to send or receive personal messages if they know the hardware store manager or owner might read their mail. A hardware store owner who informs employees that their e-mail will be monitored is communicating a policy. Hardware store owners do not inform employees that their e-mail will be monitored in order to reduce their liability or to control operating costs.

prompt: What is a key marketing function that makes products available to consumers?
explanation: Distribution. Distribution is all the activities involved in moving or transferring the ownership of goods and services from producers to consumers. Distribution activities include packaging, stock handling, transportation, warehousing, inventory control, and management of distribution. Promotion is a marketing function which communicates information about goods, services, images, or ideas to customers or clients. Communication is an exchange of information in which words and gestures are understood in the same way by both the speaker and the listener.

prompt: What indirect channel of distribution is used to reach large retailers when the producer does not want responsibility for the selling activities?
choices: Producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer
Producer to agent to retailer to consumer
explanation: Producer to agent to retailer to consumer. Some producers don't want to take the responsibility or spend the time or money to sell their own goods but are prepared to handle other marketing functions. These producers contract with an agent to sell the goods to retailers. When the producer to retailer to consumer channel is used, the producer retains control of selling activities. The producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer channel is frequently used to reach small retailers. Producer to consumer is a direct channel of distribution.

prompt: Which of the following examples demonstrates the use of satellite tracking within a distribution channel:
choices: A computer system performs warehouse functions that are usually executed by humans.
A dispatcher has current knowledge of a delivery truck's location and destination.
A technological system creates an efficient routing plan for transportation companies.
An inventory specialist enters product status information into a handheld electronic device.
explanation: A dispatcher has current knowledge of a delivery truck's location and destination. Satellite tracking is the use of satellites and technological systems that allow for the transmission of information between two parties. Satellite tracking would help a business locate a package while it is en route in order to provide an estimated arrival time to the package recipient. Computer systems that perform warehouse functions that are usually executed by humans are called artificial intelligence systems. A computer software program would be used to create routing plans for transportation companies, not a satellite tracking system. Satellites are not generally needed to enter information into an electronic device.

prompt: Tying agreements between producers and distributors might be considered illegal if they substantially limit
explanation: Competition. Competition is rivalry between two or more businesses to attract customer dollars. It should not be prevented through specific business actions such as tying agreements which require a customer to buy other products in order to obtain desired goods and services. Tying agreements are considered illegal if they substantially limit competition by preventing other distributors from obtaining and selling the same product to customers. Tying agreements are not considered illegal if they limit profitability, management, or technology.

prompt: When using the distribution function to provide good customer service, retailers take into consideration the
explanation: Differences between customers. Not all customers are the same or have the same needs. Therefore, retailers should consider the differences between customers when using the distribution function to provide good service. For example, what is good service to one customer might not be good service to another customer. For example direct-mail retailers must consider that some customers prefer overnight deliver, while other customers are satisfied with four-day service. Therefore, the retailers should offer several shipping options to accommodate different customers. Considering all the differences will help businesses distribute products in a way that meets the needs of all customers. Businesses do not need to consider the structure of the warehouse, the organization of the inventory, or the various receiving procedures when using the distribution function to provide good customer service.

prompt: A manager of a large office-furniture company is preparing an invoice for one metal desk at $265.25, a credenza at $215.50, a bookcase at $195.95, and a file cabinet at $82.50. What is the total amount of the invoice if the manager gives a 15% discount?
explanation: $645.32. The manager prepares the invoice by adding together the cost of each item of furniture ($265.25 + $215.50 + $195.95 + $82.50 = $759.20). The manager calculates the 15% discount by multiplying the total cost of the furniture by the percent of discount ($759.20 x .15 = $113.88). Then the manager subtracts the discount from the total cost to determine the total invoice amount ($759.20 - $113.88 = $645.32).

prompt: An important step in processing products for return to vendors is
explanation: Identifying reason for return. Many businesses have a return-to-vendor form that accompanies goods being returned to the vendor. These forms have space in which to write the reason that the product is being returned. This information is necessary to the vendor and to the business that is entitled to credit for the return. The business would not pay an invoice for a product that is being returned. The exact value should be indicated, not an estimated value. Returns would be shipped by routine methods rather than express.

prompt: Merchandise kept in a stockroom or warehouse is called __________ stock.
explanation: Reserve. Stock that is not needed on the sales floor at the time it is received is held in reserve until it is needed. This merchandise then replaces forward stock, the stock on the selling floor. Stock that is on back order has not been shipped from the vendor. Perpetual is a type of inventory control that keeps a constantly updated record of stock.

prompt: What is one of the disadvantages of storing additional merchandise at centralized distribution centers?
explanation: Excessive control. Many large retailers that have multiple locations store additional merchandise at centralized distribution centers. One of the disadvantages of a central distribution center is that there is more control over the process of transporting goods to the various locations. Frequently, only a few people have the authority to release goods, and there is an extensive amount of paperwork involved, which increases the amount of time it takes to distribute goods. Although excessive control is a disadvantage, there are many advantages to using a centralized distribution center. These centers usually have mechanized processing that increases efficiency, automatic marking systems that reduce pricing problems, and improved security to protect goods.

prompt: Which of the following is a risk of maintaining too small of a toy inventory:
explanation: Lost sales. Customers are usually not willing to wait for toy retailers to stock the merchandise they want to buy. Instead, they simply shop at another business that is able to fill their want. The other three alternatives are the result of maintaining too large of a toy inventory. Product obsolescence occurs when the merchandise goes out of fashion while sitting in storage. Excessive storage costs are the result of additional heating, lighting, insurance, and space requirements related to maintaining a larger than necessary inventory. Finally, the longer merchandise sits in inventory, the more times it will likely need to be handled (e.g., moved or packed) to make way for new inventory.

prompt: A method of physical inventory control in which portions of the stock are counted at regular intervals is called a __________ method.
explanation: Tickler-control. The term tickler comes from the tickler file which reminds the business when it is time to count a particular portion of stock. Visual control is looking over stock to see what needs to be reordered. A basic stock list shows the minimum amount of staple goods that should be on hand and the quantity that should be reordered. Model stock is a list of items that are always kept in inventory.

prompt: Many retailers today use computers to keep __________ track of inventory.
explanation: Perpetual. Perpetual inventory control is an inventory method which updates inventory information on a continuous basis. Most large retailers today use computers to keep perpetual track of inventory because computers can record each transaction as it occurs and adjust the inventory records immediately. Periodic is a method of inventory control in which stock is counted at certain times of the year. Manual inventory control is done by hand. Occasional is not a method of inventory control.

prompt: What risk does a retailer take when its inventory control system indicates that too little merchandise is on hand?
choices: The costs for keeping inventory will increase.
Customers may become upset about product shortages.
There is likely to be more damage to the inventory.
The inventory of clothing may become obsolete.
explanation: Customers may become upset about product shortages. When retailers do not have products on hand to meet customer demand, they risk frustrating their customers who will probably choose to shop somewhere else. The costs for keeping inventory usually decrease when there is too little merchandise on hand because the risk for theft, damage, and obsolescence goes down. It is when a retailer has a lot of merchandise in inventory (as opposed to too little) that the risk for damage becomes greater.

prompt: Why is it important for a home-improvement retailer to coordinate distribution with its promotional activities?
choices: To establish a relationship with one intermediary
To guarantee a sufficient supply of advertised items
To charge higher prices for delivery service
To arrange the most economical method of transportation
explanation: To guarantee a sufficient supply of advertised items. Home-improvement retailers coordinate distribution with their promotional activities in order to make sure that sufficient quantities of items are available when they are advertised. If a home-improvement retailer plans to promote a certain item or offer it at a special price, it must make sure that an adequate supply will be on hand to meet consumer demand. Home-improvement retailers may lose customers if they advertise items that are not available because they failed to make the necessary distribution plans. Home-improvement retailers do not coordinate distribution with promotional activities in order to charge higher prices for delivery service, arrange the most economical method of transportation, or establish a relationship with one intermediary.

prompt: What might result if a manufacturer begins to sell directly to large businesses rather than through traditional wholesalers?
explanation: Vertical channel conflict. Vertical conflict may occur among members who are on different levels of the same channel of distribution. For example, a manufacturer traditionally sells products to wholesalers who sell the products to a business. If the manufacturer starts to sell directly to the business, the wholesalers are eliminated from the channel of distribution, which might create conflict because the wholesalers are losing customers and revenue. Reverse distribution involves recycling an existing product. Horizontal conflict may occur among members who are on the same level in a channel of distribution. Exclusive distribution involves selling to only one distributor.

prompt: A product that has utility is one that is
explanation: Useful to customers. Utility is usefulness. Products with utility are capable of satisfying customer needs and wants and are useful to their purchasers. The products may be intangible, not capable of being detected through the senses, or tangible products that can be perceived through the senses. Whether the products are transferable to other customers or can be purchased on credit are not factors affecting utility.

prompt: Which of the following regulatory agencies would be concerned with price fixing and unfair competitive practices:
explanation: Federal Trade Commission. This regulatory agency was established to administer and enforce antitrust laws and laws prohibiting price fixing and unfair competitive practices. The National Labor Relations Board administers labor-management relations laws, resolves labor disputes, and prevents unfair labor practices. The Consumer Product Safety Commission sets and enforces safety standards on consumer items. The Federal Communications Commission grants licenses to radio and television stations and regulates interstate telephone and telegraph rates and services.

prompt: If a consumer chooses to go to the movies rather than to buy a new CD, then the movie theater and the CD business are
explanation: Indirect competitors. Indirect competition occurs among businesses that offer dissimilar products. Those businesses are actually competing for the same consumer dollars, even though they offer different products. The businesses are not engaged in price competition, which focuses on price to attract customers, or in prospecting, the process of identifying and locating potential clients.

prompt: Calculate the rate of unemployment in a community if there are 20,500 people in the labor force and 1,300 people are unemployed.
explanation: 6.3%. The labor force includes those who are working and those who are unemployed, but are actively looking for work. The unemployment rate is the percentage of those unemployed people in the labor force. To calculate the rate of unemployment, divide the number of unemployed by the number in the labor force (1,300 ÷ 20,500 = .063 or 6.3%). The rate of unemployment is used to analyze the condition of the economy. A low unemployment rate indicates a healthy economy, because most of the people who want to work are working. On the other hand, a high unemployment rate indicates a slowdown in the economy, with fewer goods and services produced and many people out of work.

prompt: A strong and highly valued U.S. dollar would have the following effect on the international marketplace:
explanation: Discourage U.S. exports. A strong U.S. dollar would discourage rather than encourage exporting since foreign customers would have to pay more for the goods they purchased. Decreased imports and increased exports would both be results of a weak U.S. dollar.

prompt: An example of primary data collected by a retailer to determine customer spending habits would be
choices: results of an independent research study.
a customer survey taken at the retail store.
explanation: A customer survey taken at the retail store. Primary data are original facts collected to support the research topic or to solve a specific problem. In this case, the retailer is originating its own survey to determine customers' spending habits. Customer credit reports, results from an independent research study, and statistics provided by Consumer Reports are secondary data because the data have been collected for other purposes.

prompt: One way that researchers can protect the integrity of the marketing information they collect is to
explanation: Interpret it correctly. Marketing-information managers can protect the integrity of the information they collect by interpreting it correctly and not manipulating it in such a way that it agrees with a predetermined conclusion. Protecting the integrity of marketing information is sometimes difficult because researchers often can make the information support either side of an issue depending on how they interpret it. Most researchers try to interpret the information correctly because consumers are sometimes suspicious of research findings that seem to support the opinions of the business that sponsors the research. Researchers do not protect the integrity of marketing information by reviewing it frequently, publishing it openly, or organizing it logically.

prompt: Retailers need a great deal of information in order to make effective decisions and solve specific problems. This information is usually obtained through
explanation: Marketing research. Marketing research is the systematic gathering, recording, and analyzing of data about a specific problem. Retailers use the information that is obtained through marketing research in decision making and problem-solving. Data analysis is usually a part of the research process that involves interpreting the information that has been collected. Observation is a marketing-research method that gathers data by watching consumers. Financial management is the decision making involved in allocating funds.

prompt: Which of the following data-processing methods is done quickly and does not require retailers to manually handle raw data:
explanation: Optical scanning. Optical scanning techniques allow raw data to be read electronically, often by bar codes. It translates the data into meaningful information. Computer keyboarding is a manual method of handling raw data. Cyber-opting and voice networking are not commonly used terms to describe marketing-information management methods.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of range:
choices: Most consumers buy four CDs per month.
Consumers buy an average of five CDs per month.
Consumers buy between three and seven CDs per month.
Half of all consumers buy more than five CDs per month.
explanation: Consumers buy between three and seven CDs per month. Range is the distance between the smallest and largest value in a set of responses. In the example, three was the smallest number of CDs purchased and seven was the largest number. The distance between three and seven is the range. Range is often used to describe the relation between numbers, such as the variation between the number of CDs purchased. Mean is the average, such as consumers buying an average of five CDs per month. Mode is the most common response, such as most consumers buy four CDs per month. Median is the exact middle, such as half of all consumers buying more than five CDs per month.

prompt: Advancements in technology are likely to cause a retailer to
explanation: Change its marketing strategies. Advancements in technology are one of the factors that can affect marketing strategies. Others include the actions of competitors, the influence of governmental agencies, changes in consumer attitudes, and economic changes. Advancements in technology are not likely to affect a company's product warranties, retirement plans, or employee benefits.

prompt: What is one factor that the Cost Cutter Discount Store chain considers when identifying promotional activities to include in its marketing plan?
explanation: Costs involved. An important part of a marketing plan is the promotional activities that the Cost Cutter Discount Store chain will use to inform, persuade, or remind customers of its products. When identifying these activities, the Cost Cutter Discount Store chain considers the costs involved because it has only a certain amount of money to spend on promotion. The Cost Cutter Discount Store chain wants to select the promotional activities that will reach the greatest number of potential customers for the most reasonable price. A marketing plan is concerned with promotional activities rather than safety issues, the inventory system, or wage regulations. However, these factors are an important part of the overall business plan.

prompt: What are retail businesses examining when they conduct a situational analysis during the marketing-planning process?
explanation: Environmental factors. The purpose of a situational analysis is to examine and interpret the environmental factors that affect the retail business. The environmental factors may be internal, such as a retail business's distribution system or pricing strategy, as well as external, such as the state of the economy or the number of competitors. Retail businesses examine both types of environmental factors in order to adapt to change and make effective marketing decisions. For example, if the economy is slowing down, a retail business might decide to adjust its prices to remain competitive. Physical characteristics are personal traits such as age, height, weight, etc. Personal aptitudes are a person's natural talents. Geographical changes involves changes in natural features or climate.

prompt: The primary reason for a bed and bath retailer to forecast sales is to obtain information to use in
explanation: Business planning. A bed and bath retailer uses the projected sales income to make major business decisions such as scheduling production, setting prices, purchasing materials and equipment, and hiring staff. Information used in training staff and preparing advertising copy comes from other sources within the bed and bath retailer. Analyzing past sales, rather than forecasting sales, would be helpful in evaluating salespersons.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a businessperson developing cultural sensitivity:
choices: Taking a course in ancient history
Studying road maps of various countries
explanation: Learning differences in body language. Body language includes gestures, facial expressions, tone of voice, or any other form of communicating without words. These forms of nonverbal communication have different meanings in different parts of the world. Furthermore, some gestures that are acceptable in one country are actually offensive in other countries. Businesspeople who take the time to learn the differences in body language usually are able to develop cultural sensitivity and avoid using inappropriate gestures and facial expressions. Businesspeople do not develop cultural sensitivity by practicing oral presentation skills, taking a course in ancient history, or studying road maps of various countries.

prompt: What is one way that employees who routinely deal with customers can demonstrate a customer-service mindset?
explanation: Make eye contact. Looking customers in the eye is one way of demonstrating a customer-service mindset. It shows that employees are focused on customers and their needs. Failing to make eye contact indicates indifference and could cause customers to believe employees don't care about them or their needs. Other ways of demonstrating a customer-service mindset include varying the tone of voice, rather than speaking in a monotone, and smiling at customers, rather than keeping a straight face. It is important to maintain good posture, although that doesn't mean employees should stand at attention.

prompt: How should employees give directions to customers?
explanation: Clearly. Employees should always give clear directions to customers so that the customers can understand them. Employees should speak distinctly and explain the directions in a manner that will be easy for customers to follow. Customers often become annoyed if they are given unclear directions that they do not understand. Employees should not give directions quickly, but take enough time to explain them accurately to customers. Employees should speak loud enough for customers to hear them easily. Employees should never give vague or incomplete directions.

prompt: What do coworkers who are involved in a dispute need to do before they can find a possible solution?
explanation: Identify the problem. The first step in resolving conflict involves identifying the problem. If coworkers are involved in a dispute, they need to identify exactly what the problem is before they can find a possible solution. Determining the conflict is often difficult because the parties involved may have different opinions about the problem. Once coworkers take the time to discuss the conflict and identify the exact problem, they will be in a better position to agree on a possible solution. Ignoring the situation usually makes the dispute worse and does not solve the problem. Arbitrators usually negotiate problems between management and labor. Negotiating a settlement is the last step in resolving conflict.

prompt: What is often the best way for a retailer to increase its profit?
explanation: Reduce expenses. Decreasing expenses is perhaps the best way that retailers can help to increase profit. Retailers have control over many of their expenses and can take measures to reduce them. For example, they can eliminate some free services and encourage workers to turn off lights and equipment when not being used, in order to save money on energy costs. Raising prices will not increase profits unless customers are willing to pay the higher prices. Tax rates are regulated by government. If retailers improve sales, they might increase their profits if the rate of sales is proportionately higher than the expense involved.

prompt: A system used by some retail businesses to manage the supplies needed by various departments is a __________ system.
explanation: Requisition. Stores that use requisition systems provide each department with requisition forms. The department can request the supplies it needs by listing them on the requisition form and submitting the form to the central storeroom. This system provides a record of the supplies that have been used and need to be replaced. A want slip is a customer's request for an item that is not carried by the store. Consignment is a purchase arrangement whereby products are sent to a retailer who pays for the products only upon their sale. Dollar-control is an inventory control method that tracks inventory according to its monetary value.

prompt: Which of the following is a true statement about housekeeping in a retail business:
choices: It is not an important responsibility.
It is usually a monthly activity.
It is limited to emptying trash.
explanation: It is an ongoing responsibility. Keeping the sales areas of a retail business clean and neat is not a one-time or monthly activity, but an ongoing responsibility. It can include dusting, straightening stock, picking up debris from the floor, getting rid of empty boxes, or any other light housekeeping chores that are needed. It is important to the success of the business for customers to find sales areas as neat and clean as possible.

prompt: Nonverbal communication includes body language, which often indicates the level of a person's
explanation: Enthusiasm. Your facial expressions, body posture, eye contact, personal appearance, and your actions tell others whether you are enthusiastic or indifferent. Ability, education, and intelligence cannot be measured by body language.

prompt: A retailer who discovers that an employee is stealing supplies or cash from the store might decide to dismiss and then __________ that employee.
explanation: Prosecute. An employee who is caught stealing from a retail store ultimately faces the possibility of being prosecuted for the crime and sent to prison. Most retailers dismiss employees who are caught stealing, but also may decide to take legal action if the amount that was stolen is sizeable. Stealing is not only unethical, but is also illegal and may result in criminal prosecution. A retailer would most likely dismiss, or terminate, an employee who is caught stealing rather than reassign or transfer that employee to another job or location within the business.

prompt: Pat, Jamie, Sheila, Karen, and Brent decided to work together as a group instead of separately to solve a problem. The group thought of several ideas that might help solve a particular problem. Which of the following is this group demonstrating:
explanation: Brainstorming. Brainstorming is a creative thinking technique that involves the identification of as many different ideas as possible during a certain time frame. Brainstorming is used most often in a group setting in order to generate several ideas to help solve a problem. Role-playing is the process of assuming roles and acting through a given situation. Although the group thought of ideas, they did not act them out. Experimenting is the act of testing or trying out a proposed idea or procedure. The group did not try out any of the ideas. Mental exercise, such as meditation, is the act of contemplating, reflecting, or thinking over.

prompt: When facing change, you should always try to see the __________ involved.
explanation: Benefits. Learn to look at changes in your personal life or your career as opportunities to learn and to become a better person. Focus on good outcomes of change rather than on the change itself. Have a positive attitude rather than looking for possible drawbacks or shortcomings. The side effects of change cannot be accurately predicted.

prompt: Which of the following is an action that employees can take to meet their employer's expectations of honesty:
choices: Looking for better ways to do the job
explanation: Accepting responsibility for mistakes. Employers expect their employees to have the necessary skills to do the work, but they also expect them to be honest. Being honest means not only that employees will not lie or steal, but that they will accept responsibility for their mistakes and not make excuses or blame others. Businesses respect employees who are honest and admit their mistakes because businesses realize that everyone makes mistakes from time to time. Employees who complete assignments on time are meeting their employer's expectations for dependability. Employees who help coworkers or look for better ways to do the job are exhibiting initiative.

prompt: Which of the following offers stable employment opportunities because they are usually well established and do not need to pay stockholders or investors:
explanation: Nonprofit institutions. Nonprofit institutions are businesses and organizations whose intent is to make enough money to support their mission. They are in business to help others rather than to reward stockholders, investors, or owners. They usually provide stable employment opportunities because they are well established and do not have to make a profit to continue to exist. Partnerships, corporations, and sole proprietorships are in business to earn a profit and pay stockholders, investors, and owners.

prompt: What is one of the benefits of sending an interview follow-up letter?
choices: Lets the applicant submit test scores
Reminds the interviewer of the applicant
Allows the applicant to include a résumé
explanation: Reminds the interviewer of the applicant. Applicants should send follow-up letters immediately after the interview in order to thank the interviewers for their time. Follow-up letters also remind the interviewer of the specific applicant and help to create a favorable impression. If there are several applicants with comparable qualifications, an interviewer might select the one who remembered to send a follow-up letter. An applicant's résumé, references, and test scores usually are submitted with the employment application or during the employment interview.

prompt: A product has sold well in test markets, and the developer now plans a national promotional campaign with television spots and full-page advertisements in magazines. The price of the product will probably
explanation: Increase. The price is likely to increase in order to cover the additional costs of an expensive promotional effort to introduce the product to a national market. The price is not likely to decrease, remain the same, or constantly change.

prompt: What do optical scanners read at checkout counters that helps reduce human errors in recording product price?
explanation: Universal Product Codes. Universal Product Codes (UPCs) are bar codes composed of several white and black vertical parallel lines and a row of numbers. Each item has its own distinctive UPC that contains, among other information, the price of the item. Scanning this price reduces the chance for human error associated with manual key entry. Universal vendor markings refer to a row of numbers printed on the price tag and requires an electronic wand to scan the information. Price look-ups are manually entered, and coupons are scanned as a discount to price rather than as an actual price.

prompt: One way for a retailer to accomplish its goal of selling a large volume of products is to charge __________ prices.
explanation: Low. One way for a retailer to increase its volume of sales is to charge low prices. The retailer will generate more total income because it sells more products. Low prices probably will attract more customers who will buy goods, thereby increasing sales and profits. Charging high prices may increase the dollar value of sales, but not the volume of sales. Charging competitive or moderate prices might make it more difficult to increase the volume of sales because prices are similar to those of competitors.

prompt: What product/service planning function often is expensive, but also can significantly increase sales?
explanation: Packaging. Packaging is placing the product in a protective wrap or container before it is offered for sale. Packaging is an important function of product/service planning because the package must be eye-catching in order to attract purchasers. The cost of packaging may be expensive, but studies indicate that good packaging can significantly increase sales. Labeling is attaching printed information about the product to the product. Handling is loading and unloading goods. Grading is the process of rating products according to certain established standards or characteristics.

prompt: In product/service management, a major disadvantage of rapid technological changes is the
choices: increase in customer satisfaction and profitability.
number of new products entering the market.
rate at which existing products become obsolete.
explanation: Rate at which existing products become obsolete. Technology advances so rapidly that products introduced to market are quickly being reintroduced with upgrades or changes that make the original obsolete. The problem is that many technically advanced products have a short life cycle because more advanced products take their place. Increasing the introduction of new products and improving customer awareness will increase customer satisfaction and, as a result, increase sales and profitability. These are advantages of new technology.

prompt: A computer manufacturer offers customers who pay for their computers over a period of time, the opportunity to upgrade to a new machine at the end of the contract. This is an example of an ethical solution to the problem of
explanation: Planned obsolescence. Planned obsolescence occurs when businesses continually upgrade and develop new products, which make an existing product out-of-date, thereby creating an increase in the market for new products. It is often looked upon as unethical and a means of taking advantage of the consumer. Offering an upgrade is a way to solve the problem. Overproduction, sales forecasting, and product positioning are not unethical business considerations.

prompt: In its catalogs, a retailer states: "If you are not completely satisfied with any item you buy from us at any time during your use of it, return it, and we will refund your full purchase price." This is an example of a
explanation: Guarantee on goods. Tangible products are items or goods, rather than services. A guarantee is a promise made by the seller to the consumer that the seller will refund the consumer's purchase price, if the product does not perform as expected. Therefore, the retailer is offering a guarantee on goods. A guarantee on a service would be a promise to refund the consumer's money, if the person was not satisfied with an intangible item. A warranty is a promise made by the seller to the consumer that the seller will repair or replace a product that does not perform as expected.

prompt: Colson Furniture Store advertised a deluxe video stand and bookcase in the weekend newspaper. However, the ad did not mention "limited quantities or assembly required." What government agency might charge this business with misleading advertising?
explanation: Federal Trade Commission. One of the major goals of the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) is to protect consumers. Laws administered by the FTC forbid false, misleading, or deceptive advertising of consumer products. The Federal Reserve is the central banking organization of the United States. The Federal Communications Commission grants licenses to radio and television stations and regulates interstate telephone and telegraph rates and services. The Food and Drug Administration enforces laws that protect consumer health.

prompt: A retailer can set up product lines according to which of the following methods:
explanation: Distribution. A retailer may offer any number of product lines and define them in a variety of ways. Retailers that set up product lines according to the way in which products reach the customer are using the distribution method. For example, retailers that sell products only through catalogs are using the distribution method of setting up product lines. Expansion, alteration, and contraction are product-mix strategies.

prompt: An ongoing dollar amount that buyers are permitted to order for their stores or departments is called
explanation: Open-to-buy. Open-to-buy is the amount of merchandise in dollars or units that buyers are permitted to order for their store or department during a designated time period. Stock-to-sales ratio is based on past sales figures of how fast the particular items of a department or category sell. This ratio is important to determine stock needed at the beginning of each month. Assortment plans project the variety and quantity of specific units needed by a store or department to meet customer demand. An SKU, or stockkeeping unit, is the smallest unit for which sales and stock records are kept. An SKU is assigned to each type of item in stock and includes information such as size, price, and color.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a retail business positioning a product based on the product's features and benefits:
choices: Describing similarities within a product line
explanation: Emphasizing capabilities and durability. There are several ways to position a product and one is to emphasize the product's features and benefits. A feature is a characteristic of a product, such as its specific capabilities. A benefit is an advantage that consumers receive from using a product, such as durability. By emphasizing capabilities and durability, a business is positioning a product based on its features and benefits. Positioning a product according to features and benefits does not involve advertising price line and quality, describing similarities within a product line, or promoting characteristics available from competitors.

prompt: Under which of the following circumstances should a department store plan to increase its stock:
choices: Price increases are anticipated on seasonal goods.
Cost of working capital is high.
Additional storage space is incurring inventory carrying costs.
explanation: Price increases are anticipated on seasonal goods. If a price increase is anticipated on seasonal goods, it would be wise to place large, early orders. A high cost of working capital resulting from high interest rates on borrowed money would require reduced inventory levels. If a department store has to rent additional storage space, the carrying cost could outweigh the benefit of having the additional inventory. Merchandise purchased at the end of the season may not be sold, thus the discount would not be sufficient reason to increase stock.

prompt: If the total markdown was $15.00 and initial selling price was $65.00, compute the markdown percentage.
explanation: 23%. To calculate markdown percentage, divide amount of markdown by original price: $15.00 (markdown) ÷ $65.00 (original selling price) = .23 or 23%.

prompt: If there is an increase in actual sales over planned sales, how will this affect planned purchases?
choices: Planned purchases will not be affected.
explanation: Planned purchases should be increased. Most companies expect to make purchases throughout the year. They do not use all of their open-to-buy, or funds available for purchasing, at one time. This allows them to increase or decrease purchases according to sales, which does not always mean that planned purchases should be doubled.

prompt: When determining what to buy, you should do all of the following except
choices: study industry trends, consumer demand, and retail prices.
limit items purchased to those recommended by the wholesaler.
conduct a careful study of a product's sales history.
keep in touch with vendors to observe their new lines, prices, and delivery times.
explanation: Limit items purchased to those recommended by the wholesaler. This tactic alone would not be in the best interest of the retailer. A wise buyer would study industry trends, consumer demand, and retail prices. The buyer should keep in touch with vendors to observe their new lines, prices, and delivery times as well as conduct a careful study of a product's sales history.

prompt: A list of items that shows what is always kept in inventory is called a __________ plan.
explanation: Model stock. The model stock plan reflects a store's decision as to whether it will carry a full range of items or only popular brands. A basic stock list indicates the minimum amount of stock to be kept on hand for each item and the quantity to be reordered. Tickler control is the process of counting portions of the stock at regular intervals. Reorder control uses reminder cards to let buyers know when it is time to reorder.

prompt: A sales representative for a new company that sells unusual-tasting flavors of soda is visiting a local discount store to make shoppers aware of the company's products. What promotional tool is being used if the representative hands out coupons for $1.00 off the product and entry blanks for a contest to win a trip?
explanation: Sales promotion. Sales promotion includes activities other than advertising, personal selling, and publicity that stimulate customer purchases. Coupons and contests are examples of sales promotional activities. Personal selling is planned, personalized communication that is intended to influence the purchase decision. Advertising is any paid form of nonpersonal presentation of ideas, goods, or services. Publicity is any nonpersonal presentation of ideas, goods, or services that is not paid for by the company or individual which benefits from it.

prompt: One way that promotional activities can benefit the mass media is by
explanation: Providing financial support. Promotional activities can be viewed as providing advantages or benefits to society and the mass media. The mass communication media—radio, television, newspapers, and magazines—are either partially or completely supported by promotional dollars. Without this money, financial support of the media would probably be passed along to consumers. Promotion benefits society by contributing to economic growth, supporting business activity, and helping to create jobs.

prompt: Personal selling would be a cost-effective form of promotion for which of the following products:
explanation: Scanner. Personal selling is the form of promotion that uses planned, personalized communication in order to influence purchase decisions and enhance future business opportunities. Certain industrial and retail products with hidden or complex features require technical explanation by skilled salespeople. The garden rake, soft drink, and newspaper are not complicated or sophisticated products. Consequently, personal selling would not be cost effective for these products.

prompt: The free-standing computer terminal in a retail store that allows customers to check prices and locate gift registries is often referred to as a(n)
explanation: Kiosk. A kiosk is a stand-alone structure that is located in a public place and is designed to provide information and sell products. Intranet refers to the networking of computers, often within a business, that permits the sharing of information. Virtual mall refers to the common access point of Internet store fronts. Cyber-post is not a term commonly used to describe a free-standing computer terminal, or kiosk.

prompt: The part of a print advertisement that should make the viewer want to read on is the
explanation: Headline. The headline should be written to appeal to the reader and to interest him/her in reading more of the advertisement. The body copy should expand the theme of the headline and stress the benefits of the product. The typeface refers to the design of the letters used in an advertisement.

prompt: A small retail chain that sells specialized products for sports enthusiasts is located in a resort area that receives most of its business during the summer. To increase year-round sales, management wants to use direct-mail advertising. Which of the following formats would you recommend that the retail chain use:
explanation: Niche catalogs. These specialized catalogs focus on lifestyles and hobbies and can target specific customers by using a database. Box-holder flyers are generally used to promote a business in a local area, thus not reaching the audience sought by this retailer. Cable television shopping channels usually carry well-known brands and usually require a large amount of inventory in stock to meet demands of the customers. Computer kiosks are free-standing units that are located in stores or malls for consumers to request information and order merchandise.

prompt: A good customer database makes it possible for a retailer to
explanation: Predict trends. By monitoring a customer database, a retailer is able to track the type of goods customers are buying and how much they are spending. It will tell them if customers are spending more or less and if they are affected by seasonal and price changes. Therefore, this data can help retailers predict future trends. As a result of identifying trends, a retailer might decide to offer better discounts. An existing customer database will not help a retailer find new customers or calculate profits.

prompt: What type of special event might a garden shop organize to promote a new line of garden tools and supplies to a target market?
explanation: Demonstration. A demonstration of how garden tools and supplies are used is an example of a special event. A garden shop might organize a demonstration to promote a new line of garden tools and supplies because a demonstration would be of interest to the shop's customers. Showing customers the correct way to use the tools and supplies and allowing them to participate in the demonstration will encourage customers to buy. Well-publicized demonstrations are often very effective because they attract the customers who are the most interested in that particular type of product. Celebrity appearances and sweepstakes would appeal to a wide audience rather than to customers who are interested in a specific product. A media luncheon is intended for members of the media rather than the general public.

prompt: The Sweet Treat Shop attractively arranges candy boxes in an inverted pyramid. This is an example of a __________ display arrangement.
explanation: Fan. When product is situated so that is resembles an inverted pyramid, it is called a fan display arrangement. A step arrangement displays products at different heights within the display. A pyramid arrangement has a wide base of products or cartons that narrows toward the top. A zigzag arrangement displays products in a zigzag line similar to a double reverse curve.

prompt: A retailer that allows displays of merchandise to become disarranged and dusty might cause customers to have a(n) __________ of the store.
explanation: Negative image. Displays that are disarranged, dusty, and poorly maintained often cause customers to have negative images of the store and the merchandise. Retailers should understand the importance of maintaining displays in good condition. The negative image created by poorly maintained displays may cause customers to avoid doing business with those stores. Poorly maintained displays do not cause customers to have a liberal impression, an unbiased view, or an ideal opinion of stores.

prompt: When designing a display sign, you should make sure that the left and right margins of the sign are
choices: a minimum of three inches wide.
the same width as the top margin.
the same width as the bottom margin.
explanation: Exactly the same width. The left and right margins of a display sign should match. Their maximum width should be three inches. The top margin should be one and a half times as wide as the left and right margins. The bottom margin should be twice as wide as the side margins.

prompt: Which of the following types of display aids might be supplied by a vendor:
explanation: Point-of-purchase rack. Customers make their own selections from these self-service displays which contain only the vendor's products. Vendors would not supply mannequins, which are expensive and can be used for competitive products. Lighting fixtures and plants enhance displays, but they would not be supplied by a vendor.

prompt: Retail businesses that do not have adequate in-house staff to coordinate large promotional events often must pay for the services of
explanation: Outside agencies. Coordinating large promotional events is an important responsibility that may require the retail business to engage the assistance of outside agencies. Many businesses do not have sufficient in-house staff to handle the everyday promotional activities as well as special events. The responsibility for coordinating large promotional events would not be given to part-time employees or executives even though they are already on the payroll. Retail businesses seldom have volunteers on staff.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a tangible item that can be sold:
explanation: Computer. A computer has the characteristics of a tangible item. Tangible items are those that can be touched, smelled, tasted, and/or seen. A car wash, a haircut, and a lawyer's advice are all services.

prompt: When customers believe that salespeople know the facts about the products they sell, customers view the salespeople as having
explanation: Credibility. Salespeople who have complete product knowledge and can communicate the positive attributes and applications of their products to customers will be seen as highly credible and trustworthy. These salespeople may also be tactful, have a sense of humor, and possess a sense of values, but it is their product knowledge that creates credibility.

prompt: How can a reciprocal sales arrangement between a buyer and seller create an unethical situation?
choices: Ethical issues can occur when the reciprocity hurts or eliminates competition.
Reciprocal sales arrangements usually result when a breach of warranty occurs.
Ethical issues usually occur when the reciprocity is technological in nature.
Reciprocal sales arrangements almost always create price discrimination.
explanation: Ethical issues can occur when the reciprocity hurts or eliminates competition. Reciprocal sales arrangements are agreements between two parties that they will buy products from each other. Reciprocal sales agreements do not always create ethical dilemmas; however, problems can occur when the two parties deliberately try to eliminate competition. Price discrimination occurs when a seller has different pricing structures for similar customers. Reciprocal sales agreements do not necessarily create price discrimination. A breach of warranty occurs when the quality or performance of a product is misrepresented by the seller. Reciprocal sales arrangements can occur with any type of business. Therefore, technological businesses are not any more likely to experience ethical dilemmas when engaging in reciprocal selling arrangements than other types of businesses.

prompt: What federal regulations affect a business's sales activities by promoting competition and restricting monopolies?
explanation: Antitrust laws. A variety of federal antitrust laws exist that are intended to promote competition among businesses and prevent the formation of monopolies. These laws affect a business's sales activities because they make certain actions illegal such as price fixing and price discrimination. Businesses that violate antitrust laws are subject to severe fines and penalties. Consumer protection legislation, advertising rules, and bait-and-switch regulations do not promote competition and restrict monopolies.

prompt: One way that salespeople can obtain information about the products they sell is by reading
explanation: Company catalogs. A great deal of product information is given in product catalogs, bulletins, manuals, and other promotional materials. For example, a company catalog might describe the construction and durability of a pair of hiking boots and explain that these features provide comfort and support. Salespeople can use this information to sell the benefits of the boots to customers. News magazines contain information of general interest to the public. Professional journals contain information about topics of interest to people in a certain profession rather than information about specific products. Industry statistics do not provide product information.

prompt: Many stores sell a line of inexpensive, unbranded merchandise. These products are known as __________ brands.
explanation: Generic. These products are unbranded, i.e., the label simply says "paper towels." These products are inexpensive alternatives to brand-name goods. Specific brand names are associated with national, private, and middlemen brands.

prompt: The selling process begins and ends with the
explanation: Customer. The salesperson's job in the selling process is to consider the needs and wants of the customer at all phases of selling, from approaching the customer to reaffirming the buyer-seller relationship after the sale. The product offered should be capable of meeting the customer's needs or wants. The producer helps to begin the selling process by creating products that can be sold.

prompt: The person who writes a check is called the
explanation: Maker. Another term for a person who writes a check is drawer. The person or business to whom the check is written is the payee. A beneficiary is a person designated in a will or insurance policy to receive certain funds. A checker is a cashier.

prompt: If a cashier added two rolls of dimes and a roll of nickels to a cash drawer that contained $69.50, how much change would be in the drawer?
explanation: $81.50. To determine the amount of change in the cash drawer after the addition of the rolls of coins, first determine the value of the coins. Since each roll of dimes is worth $5, multiply to determine the total value of the dimes ($5 x 2 = $10). A roll of nickels contains 40 nickels and is worth $2. Add the amount in the cash drawer to the coins to calculate the amount of change in the drawer ($69.50 + $10 + $2 = $81.50).

prompt: One reason that large discount stores might not offer home delivery service is because
choices: most orders are too bulky to deliver by traditional transportation methods.
it is more difficult for customers to return unwanted items.
most products that discount stores sell are highly perishable.
it can be difficult to plan, execute, and control such services.
explanation: It can be difficult to plan, execute, and control such services. Because of the volume of business and the inconsistency of consumer shopping habits, delivery service is not offered by many discount stores. In addition, delivery service can be very expensive. Offering delivery service entails the purchase or lease of a vehicle, vehicle maintenance, insurance, fuel, and driver's salary, which are substantial costs. Although discount stores may carry perishable products, it cannot be assumed that most items are perishable. Store management determines product return policies, which vary from store to store or chain to chain. Generally, delivery methods do not influence return policies. Since order size varies by each customer's needs, it cannot be assumed that most orders are too bulky to deliver.

prompt: Which of the following actions should be avoided when preparing gift certificates:
explanation: Cross out errors. When an error has been made in filling out a gift certificate, the preparer should void the gift certificate and prepare a new one. Handwriting should be neat and legible so that the name and amount are easy to read. It is also essential that information be accurately recorded and the spelling of names verified.

prompt: Businesses whose employees regularly make mistakes while taking telephone orders are likely to
explanation: Lose customers. Customers expect their telephone orders to be processed correctly and efficiently. Businesses whose employees regularly make mistakes while taking telephone orders might eventually lose customers who are dissatisfied with the poor service. Customers may take their business elsewhere if their telephone orders are regularly processed incorrectly. Businesses should take steps to remedy the problem of telephone order mistakes rather than stopping the service or computerizing the system. Increasing prices to cover the costs of the mistakes may lose more customers.

prompt: George received a jacket for his birthday but has decided to exchange it. He has a receipt for the jacket priced at $79.95 plus 4.5% tax, and he wants to exchange it for a sale item priced at $59.95 plus tax. What is the appropriate action for the salesperson to take?
choices: Make the exchange and refund George the difference of $20.90
Allow George to exchange the jacket and refund him $20.00
Round the tax to 5% and refund George $21.00
Tell George that store policy dictates it must be an even exchange
explanation: Make the exchange and refund George the difference of $20.90. This is the difference in the prices of the jackets including tax. George has the original receipt, so the store should refund him the difference and not make it an even exchange. Refunding George the $20 would not include tax. Some states do charge tax in fractions of a cent; the amount should not be rounded up but charged at the rate of 4.5%.
